title: How to create a social media viral video
content:
Every social media marketer has heard it: “How do we go viral?” The question is understandable because a viral video delivers audience growth, brand awareness and cultural relevance in a single moment. But virality is a byproduct of great content strategy, not a strategy itself.
The brands that consistently create shareable, high-performing video understand what drives engagement before they hit record, and they have a plan for what happens after a video takes off.
In this guide, you’ll get expert insight on the elements that make videos spread, how to create content built for reach across every major platform and how to manage the momentum when a video breaks through.
Rapid, high-volume sharing across social media platforms defines a viral video, and the threshold for virality varies significantly by platform.
Virality is rooted in emotion, identity and the human drive to share experiences
Every platform, including TikTok, Instagram Reels, YouTube Shorts and X (formerly Twitter), rewards different formats, behaviors and audience expectations.
Creating a viral video requires strategic groundwork: clear goals, audience insight and a production brief before you hit record
Discoverability tactics like short-form video, captions, trend-riding and hashtag strategy amplify reach after publishing
Measuring viral video performance turns a one-time spike into a repeatable content strategy
Managing the inbox surge, team workload and sentiment during a viral moment requires a plan in place before it happens
A viral video is content that spreads rapidly across social media platforms by generating an unusually high volume of shares, comments and views in a short period of time. The result: massive audience reach that organic posting alone rarely achieves.
There’s no universal view count that defines a viral video because the threshold shifts as social media usage grows. On TikTok specifically, 250,000 views signals mildly viral, one million views is medium viral and five million views within three to seven days is considered fully viral.
Virality isn’t random. It’s rooted in emotion and the human drive to connect. Research on why people share content online points to three core motivations:
Entertainment and value: People share content that makes others smile, laugh or feel something worth passing on.
Identity: Sharing content signals who we are and what we stand for.
Relationship building: Content becomes a social currency—a way to strengthen connections with others.
Ask yourself: what was the last video you shared? That video likely surprised you, made you laugh or sparked a strong reaction. That emotional trigger is the engine behind every viral video, and it’s the starting point for any brand serious about creating one.
Viral videos are not accidents. They share a consistent set of characteristics that make them easy to watch, impossible to ignore and worth passing on. Here are the core elements that appear across virtually every piece of content that spreads at scale:
A strong hook: The first two to three seconds determine everything. Viral videos earn attention immediately through a surprising visual, a direct question or an unexpected opening that makes stopping feel involuntary.
Emotional resonance: Content spreads when it makes people feel something, whether laughter, surprise, awe, nostalgia or recognition. The stronger the emotional response, the stronger the impulse to share.
Relatability: Viral videos tap into shared experiences. When viewers see themselves in a piece of content, sharing it becomes a way of saying “this is me” to their own network.
Brevity and clarity: The most-shared videos deliver a single, clear idea without waste. Concision is not a limitation; it’s a prerequisite.
Platform fit: Format, aspect ratio, audio and pacing all need to match the platform where the video lives. A video built for TikTok behaves differently than one built for YouTube Shorts.
Shareability by design: The best viral videos are built with sharing as an outcome, not an afterthought. That means giving viewers a reason to tag someone, repost or send it directly.
Timeliness or universality: Viral content either taps into a cultural moment at the right time or speaks to a feeling so universal it’s always relevant. Both work, but each requires a different production approach.
Every platform rewards different behavior, different formats and different audience expectations. Building for the platform in front of you is what separates a lucky spike from repeatable momentum.
TikTok is built for discovery. According to the 2026 Sprout Social Content Benchmarks Report, TikTok delivers the highest engagement rate of any platform at 1.75%, and 71% of marketers are increasing their investment there, more than any other social media platform. TikTok is also the top channel for product discovery among Gen Z, with 49% of Gen Z consumers turning to the platform first. If your goal is reach, this is where fast momentum starts.
Lead with the payoff: Hook viewers in the first two seconds or lose them entirely.
Use trends with purpose: Native trends work when they serve your story, not as filler.
Prioritize entertainment: Entertaining content drives engagement by a significant margin over every other content type on TikTok.
Instagram rewards content that stops the scroll and earns a share. With a 1.61% engagement rate across 376,000 posts analyzed in the 2026 Sprout Social Content Benchmarks Report, Reels remain a high-return format for brands that pair short-form creativity with platform-native execution.
Open strong: Your first frame determines whether anyone watches the second.
Design for saves and shares: These signals drive algorithmic reach far beyond your existing audience.
Repurpose with intention: Winning short-form concepts travel well across platforms when you adapt the edit, not just the caption.
YouTube has evolved into a destination for product education, with 24% of consumers turning to the platform to find new products. Short-form video now outperforms long-form for brand interaction, which means your expertise does not require a 10-minute production budget to build visibility. 56% of marketers already plan to increase their investment in YouTube in 2026 and even those who don’t find success by cross-posting short-form video from other social media platforms.
Build around searchable topics: YouTube functions as a search engine; treat your titles accordingly.
Keep framing direct: Concise, clear Shorts outperform vague or meandering content.
Connect to a series: Short videos that ladder up to broader content themes compound in reach over time.
On X, speed and a sharp point of view win. Videos that react to live moments or cultural shifts move fast when the timing is precise and the message is impossible to ignore.
Post into active conversations: Timing relative to the news cycle matters more than production quality.
Keep the message direct: One clear idea per video outperforms anything that tries to do too much.
Write copy that demands a response: The video earns the view; the caption earns the reply.
Stop chasing a generic viral formula. Build for the platform, the audience and the moment. That’s how a viral video becomes a repeatable strategy.
Making a viral video starts with strategy, not luck. Define your goals, understand your audience and build a production plan before you hit record. Then optimize every element, from your opening hook to your distribution platform, to maximize reach and shareability.
Sprout Social’s video team creates content that reaches large audiences consistently. Here are the expert steps you can apply to your own video production right now.
Knowing you want something to go viral isn’t enough for a solid social media marketing strategy . You need to know exactly why you want your video to go viral and what business outcome it drives.
Are you building brand awareness, growing your following or generating conversions? Each goal requires a different video approach for audiences at different stages of the funnel. Lock in your goals before production begins.
A video without audience insight falls flat every time. To create content that performs with your target audience and beyond, you need to know what resonates with them and what compels them to share.
Build social media personas and an empathy map to surface what grabs your audience’s attention and what they actively seek out online. According to the 2026 Sprout Social Content Benchmarks Report, 60% of TikTok users engage most with short-form video, which proves that format preferences are audience-specific and data-driven.
A creative strategy brief and storyboard align your entire team from content to production around a single, cohesive vision. Without one, messaging fractures and brand consistency suffers. Your brief should cover:
Working title: Guides the overall concept and creative direction.
Description: What the video is about and what purpose it serves.
Key items to include: Specific points or messages the video must hit.
Related content: Existing assets you can reference or incorporate.
Platforms: Which social media platforms will host the video and what format versions each requires.
Video format: Vertical or horizontal, based on platform and audience behavior.
Keywords: Critical for platforms like YouTube where SEO drives discovery.
Important hashtags and mentions : Essential for trends and partnerships.
Calls to action: What you want your audience to do after watching.
Every viral video grabs attention in the first three seconds, or it loses the viewer entirely. Use the word “you” within the first five seconds: research shows that direct address in the opening moments drives higher retention rates. Other proven ways to open with impact:
Create a plot twist or defy expectations immediately
Open with a hook such as a question, a bold claim or a numbered list
Make your content instantly relatable to your audience’s lived experience
Use attention-grabbing audio or music that fits the platform’s culture
Drop the promotional tone entirely and entertain first
As viral videos skew shorter, your story needs to land fast. Choose a universal context, something like “Monday Mood,” that your audience recognizes instantly, so you skip the backstory and get straight to the payoff.
Play to familiar tropes, then subvert them. That tension between expectation and surprise is what drives shares. Relatable, emotionally resonant storytelling is the engine behind every video that spreads beyond its original audience.
Creating a great viral video is only half the battle. Getting it in front of the right audience is where discoverability strategy takes over. These eight tactics give your video the best chance of reaching a wider audience and earning the shares that drive viral momentum.
Short-form video is the content type consumers most want from brands, and the data backs it up. According to the 2026 Sprout Social Content Benchmarks Report, short-form video under 60 seconds drives the highest engagement rates across TikTok and Instagram. Viewers who watch your entire video send a powerful signal to platform algorithms, which reward that completion with broader organic reach.
Captions do two things at once: they make your content accessible and they keep viewers watching when sound isn’t an option. Most people scroll social media in silent environments, so captions are the difference between a viewer staying or scrolling past. More viewers watching means more shares, and more shares means more reach.
Trend-riding works best when you move early. Platforms like TikTok are where trends are born and jumping on a rising trend before it peaks positions your brand as a trendsetter rather than a follower. Monitor your For You page, Instagram Reels feed and trending hashtags daily—then put your own brand spin on whatever you find.
If you want a faster signal, Sprout Social’s Feeds feature lets you monitor Twitter lists, Instagram content and RSS sources from a single dashboard, so your team spots rising conversations before they peak, without toggling between platforms. Trend awareness is a competitive advantage. The faster your team sees it, the sooner you move.
Your video title, description and caption are the first things both an algorithm and a viewer read. Strong, optimized copy explains what your video delivers, builds curiosity and improves search visibility. For YouTube especially, video SEO is a direct driver of reach—treat every title and description as a search asset, not an afterthought.
Strategic hashtags connect your video to the audiences already searching for that content on YouTube and TikTok . Use hashtags that are directly relevant to your video’s topic, not just whatever is trending. Relevance drives qualified views; qualified views drive shares.
Publishing is the starting line, not the finish line. Build a cross-platform promotion plan that puts your video in front of your audience wherever they spend time. Here are the most effective ways to amplify reach after publishing:
Share your video link in posts across Facebook, X (formerly Twitter) and LinkedIn
Create Instagram Stories with a direct link to your YouTube or TikTok video
Cut short preview clips from longer videos and post them on other platforms to drive traffic back to the original
Use your content calendar to schedule cross-platform promotion in advance
Use Sprout Social’s reporting and analytics to identify which platforms hold your most active and engaged audience, then prioritize promotion there first.
No single video builds an audience. Consistent posting teaches platform algorithms what your content is about and signals to viewers that you’re worth following. Post regularly, experiment with formats and trends and treat every video as data.
Each one tells you more about what your audience wants next. According to the 2026 Sprout Social Content Benchmarks Report, brands that post consistently on TikTok see compounding engagement gains over time.
Consistency also means posting at the right time. Sprout Social’s ViralPost® feature analyzes your specific audience’s behavior to automatically identify the optimal times to publish—so your video lands when your audience is most likely to watch, engage and share. Stop guessing at your posting schedule. Let your own data make the call.
Engagement is a two-way street. Comment on other brands’ content, respond to your own TikTok comments and build genuine relationships with communities you want to reach. Brand-to-brand interactions in comment sections regularly generate their own viral moments, and that visibility is free. Just keep your brand voice consistent and your tone respectful at all times.
Views get attention. Measurement gets budget. A viral moment means nothing if you can’t explain what it delivered or replicate it.
Real performance analysis turns a one-time spike into a repeatable strategy. Here’s what to track.
Focus on the signals that show whether people paid attention, cared enough to act and stayed engaged long enough for the algorithm to keep pushing your content.
Views and reach: understand how far the video traveled across networks and whether it broke beyond your existing audience
Watch time and completion rate: see whether the content held attention from start to finish—high completion rates are the clearest signal to platform algorithms that your video deserves wider distribution
Shares and saves: measure how strongly the video resonated—shares extend reach; saves signal intent to return, which platforms weigh heavily in their ranking logic
Comments: assess conversation quality and audience sentiment—not just volume
Follower growth, profile visits and clicks: connect the awareness spike directly to business action and use these to report ROI to leadership
Once a video starts moving, your team needs one place to see what happened across every channel and what to do next. Sprout Social’s cross-network reporting lets you compare post performance across platforms, identify patterns in your highest-engagement videos and track how momentum translates into audience growth and measurable business impact.
Use Sprout Social’s Post Performance Report to break down exactly which video elements drove reach and engagement, including format, length, publish time and caption structure, so you replicate what worked and cut what didn’t. Tag your video content in Sprout to group posts by campaign or content type, then compare performance across tags to build a data-backed blueprint for your next video.
Don’t admire the spike. Learn from it, report on it and build the next win faster.
Going viral is exhilarating and immediately overwhelming. Millions of views and thousands of new followers arrive alongside thousands of inbox messages. Without a plan, critical conversations get buried and opportunities disappear.
Here’s how to stay in control when your viral video takes off:
A viral moment floods your inbox fast. Check your social inboxes hourly instead of a few times a day and extend your monitoring beyond standard business hours. Viral content runs 24/7, and a crisis that goes unaddressed for 12 hours compounds quickly.
One centralized inbox is non-negotiable during a viral moment. In Sprout Social’s Smart Inbox, you see and respond to messages across all social media platforms, save top-priority messages, identify volume spikes, assign messages to teammates and more—all from a single view.
Checking your inbox more frequently only works if you have the bandwidth to do it. During a message spike, distribute the workload across your team before burnout sets in.
Alert your customer care teams: Communicate the volume spike immediately and set expectations for more frequent monitoring.
Build pre-written response templates: Create customizable, ready-to-use replies for common questions to standardize your brand voice and cut response time.
Monitor in shifts after hours: Divide extended monitoring into shifts so no single person carries the full load.
If you have no one to step in, start training backup monitors now. Protecting your team from burnout is a long-term strategy, not an afterthought.
Not every message carries equal weight. A customer question and a comment that could spiral into a crisis both demand faster attention than a generic reaction.
Use social listening to quickly surface overall sentiment and isolate high-priority conversations. In Sprout Social’s Smart Inbox, filter by specific keywords and accounts to surface messages from key influencers or flag potential issues before they escalate.
Take it further with Sprout Social’s Listening tool to track brand sentiment in real time, identify accounts with large followings talking about your content and spot the language people use when engaging with your viral video.
Your social media crisis plan applies to viral moments—even positive ones. A defined communication chain means your team acts in seconds, not hours.
If a crisis surfaces amid your viral moment, getting ahead of it early contains the damage. If something immensely positive happens, like a major influencer engaging with your content, a designated point person ensures you capitalize on it immediately. Time is the only resource you can’t recover on social.
Once the initial wave settles, extend your momentum by building on what worked. When managing the viral “penguin field trips” campaign at Shedd Aquarium, the team kept the campaign alive by taking penguins to meet new animals, experimenting with other animals on field trips and eventually bringing the penguins to locations across the city.
Each iteration used the same proven content format in a fresh context, generating multiple viral moments within a single campaign. Identify the specific elements that drove your original success, then build new content around them rather than chasing an entirely new idea.
A viral video brings a surge of views and new followers, but it’s not a strategy. Sustainable growth comes from building a consistent content engine and a loyal digital community.
Instead of chasing a single viral moment, focus on what drives long-term impact: a content strategy that compounds over time. Think of going viral as a bonus, not the foundation.
Consistent posting cadence that keeps your audience engaged week over week
Content that reflects your brand’s values and resonates with your specific community
A feedback loop that uses analytics to refine what works and double down on it
Viral moments are the cherry on top. Strategy builds the sundae.
The path to a viral video starts with one decision: publish. Every brand that has ever gone viral made that choice first.
Build your video marketing strategy around consistent publishing, audience-first storytelling and data-driven iteration. That combination drives reach, builds brand awareness and puts you in position to break through more than once.

A viral video is a piece of video content that spreads rapidly across social media platforms through an unusually high volume of shares, views, comments and repeat engagement in a short period of time. Viral videos consistently tap into emotion, cultural timing, relatability or utility, and they’re designed, consciously or not, to make sharing feel natural. Virality is not a random event. It’s the result of content connecting with an audience so strongly that passing it on feels like an instinct.
How do social media marketers find viral trends on TikTok?
Marketers find viral trends on TikTok by monitoring repeated formats, sounds, hashtags and conversations before they reach peak saturation. The For You page is the fastest native signal, but teams that move fastest use tools like Sprout Social’s Listening and Feeds to surface rising conversations across platforms from a single view. The rule is simple: spot the pattern early, choose the trends that fit your brand and audience, then move before the window closes.
Can a brand plan to go viral or does it happen by chance?
A brand cannot guarantee that a video goes viral, but it builds meaningfully toward that outcome through deliberate strategy. Strong hooks, clear and emotionally resonant storytelling, platform-native formatting and consistent publishing all increase the probability significantly. Chance still plays a role, but strategy narrows the gap between luck and repeatability. The brands that go viral most often are the ones that publish consistently and learn from every piece of content they put out.
Measuring the ROI of a viral video starts with attention metrics like reach, views and watch time, then moves to engagement signals like shares, saves and comments that indicate genuine resonance. From there, connect the viral moment to business outcomes: follower growth, profile visits, website clicks and conversions that leadership can tie to revenue or pipeline. A viral video that drives views but no downstream action is reach without return. The goal is to connect the spike to outcomes your organization actually cares about and to use that data to inform what you produce next.
